[[★ Troponin I (slide 72a, shown in class, not in the posted deck): standard troponin I abnormal above 0.04 ng/mL; high-sensitivity troponin I 99th percentile 12 ng/L in women, 20 ng/L in men]]; troponin I is heart-specific (troponins are proteins of cardiac and skeletal muscle, none in smooth muscle); [[★ a rule-OUT tool]], and one draw means two (watch for a rise). Risk scores GRACE, TIMI (Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction), PURSUIT, HEART (History, ECG, Age, Risk factors, Troponin). [[★ TIMI 3 or higher justifies an early invasive approach]]; HEART bands and MACE (major adverse cardiac event) percentages are not tested
fields.treatment: High-intensity statin (atorvastatin, rosuvastatin) for all ACS regardless of LDL (low-density lipoprotein), started before discharge
fields.mortality: Estimated by the risk scores; the HEART and TIMI (Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction) outcome percentages on slides 34 and 72 are not tested

conditions.name: Unstable angina
conditions.prof_note: Troponin separates unstable angina (normal) from NSTEMI (elevated); oxygen only if SpO2 <91%

fields.name: Unstable angina (UA)
fields.definition: Change in a patient's stable angina, considered ACS (acute coronary syndrome): occurs at rest, new-onset and activity-limiting, or increasing (more discomfort, more often)
fields.etiology: Change in stable angina (plaque rupture); the Braunwald classification on slide 54 (mis-cited "APACHE II") was brushed past and is not tested
fields.risk_factors: TIMI (Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction) criteria: age ≥65; ≥3 CAD (coronary artery disease) risk factors; known stenosis >50%; aspirin in past 7 days; ≥2 angina episodes in 24 h; ST deviation ≥0.5 mm; elevated marker
fields.pathology: Not covered in the lecture
fields.clinical: Pain at rest; nitroglycerin usually (not always) helps
fields.diagnosis: Nonspecific ECG (electrocardiogram) changes (usually inverted T waves) with [[★ NORMAL troponin]] (troponin separates UA from NSTEMI (non-ST-elevation MI)); stress-test ST depression or T inversion; nuclear stress: reversible defect = ischemia, fixed = infarction; TIMI (Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction) 3 or higher → early invasive approach
fields.treatment: Medical emergency, same as NSTEMI: chewable aspirin, beta-blocker, IV nitrates; DAPT (dual antiplatelet therapy: aspirin + clopidogrel) ± anticoagulation; MONA (morphine, oxygen, nitroglycerin, aspirin), [[★ oxygen only if SpO2 <91%]]. After stabilization: left heart catheterization/angiography, balloon angioplasty, PCI (percutaneous coronary intervention) with stent. Post-PCI: DAPT, statin, ACE (angiotensin-converting enzyme) inhibitor, anticoagulant if indicated; [[★ missing DAPT in the first 6 weeks → 50% risk of sudden in-stent restenosis]] (the DAPT durations on slides 52 and 83 disagree and are not tested); exercise as tolerated, low-salt/low-fat diet, follow-up
fields.mortality: TIMI (Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction) 3–7 needs ICU (intensive care unit) or emergent revascularization; the percentage table (slide 72) and Braunwald prognosis (slide 54) are not tested

conditions.name: NSTEMI
conditions.prof_note: ST depression >1 mm and/or T-wave inversion in two or more consecutive leads with elevated troponin

fields.name: NSTEMI (non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction); non-ST elevation ischemia
fields.definition: MI (myocardial infarction) diagnosed by ECG (electrocardiogram) changes + ischemic symptoms + elevated troponin/high-sensitivity troponin
fields.etiology: Not covered in the lecture
fields.pathology: Subendocardial ischemia → ST depression
fields.clinical: Signs and symptoms of ischemia; nitroglycerin may help the pain
fields.diagnosis: [[★ Slide 47: ST depression >1 mm and/or T-wave inversion in ≥2 consecutive leads + ELEVATED troponin]] (what separates it from unstable angina); troponin I abnormal above 0.04 ng/mL (high-sensitivity 12 ng/L women, 20 ng/L men). Slide 86's "ST inversion (>1 mm)" is a deck error (ST segments are depressed; T waves invert)
fields.treatment: Treated the same as unstable angina (see that card)
fields.mortality: TIMI (Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction) 3 or higher → early invasive approach (percentages not tested)

conditions.name: STEMI (transmural MI)
conditions.prof_note: Lead groups name the artery (II, III, aVF = RCA); ST depression V1–V3 = posterior, get V7–V9; new LBBB = STEMI equivalent; ECG within 10 min, door-to-balloon <90 min

fields.name: STEMI (ST-elevation myocardial infarction); transmural myocardial infarction (MI)
fields.definition: Myocardial necrosis with ST elevation in ≥2 consecutive leads not quickly reversed by nitroglycerin, reciprocal ST depression, [[★ new LBBB (left bundle branch block) = STEMI equivalent]], Q waves. Slide 65 adds "elevated cardiac markers must be present"; in class he said troponin is not required (it may not have risen yet), so this is not keyed
fields.etiology: Coronary occlusion; LAD (left anterior descending) most common culprit (40–50%), RCA (right coronary artery) 30–40%, left circumflex 15–20%
fields.pathology: Transmural ischemia → ST elevation; ECG (electrocardiogram) evolution: hyperacute T/ST elevation (minutes–hours) → T inversion + Q (hours–1 day) → Q + coronary T (1 week) → Q wave (months)
fields.clinical: Typical and referred chest pain as for ACS (acute coronary syndrome)
fields.diagnosis: [[★ ECG (electrocardiogram) within 10 min of arrival]]: ST elevation >1 mm in ≥2 consecutive leads. Localization: [[★ inferior II/III/aVF → RCA (right coronary artery)]] (and/or circumflex); lateral I/aVL/V5–V6 → circumflex or LAD (left anterior descending) diagonal; anterior/septal V1–V4 → LAD (V4 is anterior); [[★ posterior = ST depression V1–V3, confirmed with posterior leads V7–V9]]; right ventricular V1/V4R. Pathologic Q waves = infarct already happened. Slide 62's other rows and V2–V3 cut-offs are self-study
fields.treatment: Chewable aspirin; activate cath team for PCI (percutaneous coronary intervention); then ticagrelor/prasugrel/clopidogrel + heparin drip; nitroglycerin (sublingual/paste/infusion); beta-blocker if no bradycardia; [[★ if PCI ≥2 h away give thrombolytics within 30 min of arrival]] (tenecteplase most common; also alteplase, reteplase, streptokinase, anistreplase, lanoteplase); [[★ door-to-balloon <90 min]]; GP (glycoprotein) IIb/IIIa inhibitors have fallen out of favor. PCI (angioplasty, atherectomy, stent) or CABG (coronary artery bypass graft: mammary or radial ARTERY first, great saphenous vein only if an artery cannot be used). Post-MI: [[★ beta-blocker improves survival; calcium channel blockers do not]] (diltiazem/verapamil only with preserved LV function); high-intensity statin for all ACS before discharge; ACE (angiotensin-converting enzyme) inhibitor with reduced LV function; aspirin; clopidogrel after stent; warfarin for large anterior MI. Oxygen only if SpO2 <91%; [[★ no nitroglycerin within 24 h of a PDE (phosphodiesterase) inhibitor]] (ask women too: pulmonary arterial hypertension)
fields.mortality: Complications: post-infarction ischemia, heart failure, myocardial rupture, ventricular aneurysm, thromboembolism, pericarditis (Dressler syndrome, post-MI pericarditis), cardiogenic shock (more common with left-sided MI), arrhythmias; LV (left ventricular) involvement → higher mortality; beta-blockers improve survival

conditions.name: Right ventricular infarct
conditions.prof_note: Do NOT give nitroglycerin in a right ventricular infarct ("you will kill somebody")

fields.name: Right ventricular (RV) infarct
fields.definition: RCA (right coronary artery) occlusion affecting the inferior and posterior left ventricular wall and septum, extending into the RV in 15–30%
fields.etiology: Occlusion of the RCA (right coronary artery)
fields.epidemiology: RV extension in 15–30% of RCA (right coronary artery) occlusions
fields.pathology: Preload-dependent RV (right ventricle): ↓ preload reduces Frank-Starling effect → RV failure (right-sided heart failure)
fields.clinical: Not covered in the lecture
fields.diagnosis: STEMI chart: ST elevation V1 and V4R, reciprocal depression I and aVL; culprit RCA (right coronary artery); RCA supplies the AV (atrioventricular) node → dysrhythmias
fields.treatment: [[★ DO NOT GIVE nitroglycerin]] (slide 63; said three times in class): dropping preload loses the Frank-Starling push of the RV, output falls and the patient goes into shock. Slide 73's "caution in inferior MIs (right sided) with evidence of CHF" was never read and is not keyed; the rule is for right ventricular involvement, not every inferior MI (only 15–30% of RCA occlusions reach the RV)

conditions.name: Sudden cardiac death
conditions.prof_note: Ventricular fibrillation is the most common cause; the first manifestation of CAD in over 20% ("one in five")

fields.name: Sudden cardiac death
fields.definition: Not covered in the lecture
fields.etiology: [[★ Most common: ventricular fibrillation]]; also LVH (left ventricular hypertrophy), hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, hypoxia, electrolyte abnormalities
fields.epidemiology: [[★ First manifestation of CAD (coronary artery disease) in >20% of patients]]
fields.risk_factors: Sudden death in a first-degree relative (listed as a CAD (coronary artery disease) risk factor)
fields.pathology: Not covered in the lecture
fields.clinical: Not covered in the lecture
fields.diagnosis: Not covered in the lecture
fields.treatment: Not covered in the lecture

conditions.name: Vasospastic (Prinzmetal) angina
conditions.prof_note: Gold standard: ergonovine or acetylcholine provocation at angiography, relieved by nitroglycerin; calcium channel blocker first-line

fields.name: Vasospastic angina; Prinzmetal angina; variant angina; coronary vasospasm angina
fields.definition: Angina due to coronary artery vasospasm, occurring at rest and responding to nitroglycerin
fields.etiology: Vasospasm in normal or diseased coronaries; drug triggers: cocaine, ephedrine, marijuana, alcohol, amphetamine, triptans
fields.pathology: Vasospasm without high-grade stenosis on arteriography
fields.clinical: Recurrent chest pain at rest, mostly midnight to 8 am; gradual onset/offset, 5–15 min (may last longer); typical chest pain
fields.diagnosis: ECG (electrocardiogram): transient ST elevation during an episode (transient ischemic ST changes in multiple leads, <15 min) that resolves (slide 90, as described in class); slide 91's "T-wave inversion; maybe ST depression" is not keyed. No high-grade stenoses. [[★ Gold standard: spasm on angiography provoked by ergonovine or acetylcholine, relieved by nitroglycerin]]
fields.treatment: Stop smoking; nitrates for symptoms; [[★ FIRST-LINE calcium channel blockers]] (diltiazem, amlodipine); AVOID nonselective beta-blockers, aspirin, triptans

fields.name: Microvascular angina (formerly cardiac syndrome X); the slide also lists MINOCA (myocardial infarction with non-obstructive coronary arteries). Caveat: in standard usage MINOCA requires an infarction and microvascular angina does not; the deck (and the lecture) treat them as one, and no question asks you to separate them
fields.definition: Angina with ST changes, possibly elevated biomarkers, but normal coronary arteries on angiogram
fields.etiology: Proposed: endothelial dysfunction, myocardial ischemia, insulin resistance/diabetes, abnormal autonomic control, altered cardiac sensitivity, estrogen deficiency, altered pain perception
fields.epidemiology: More frequent in females; often associated with stress or anxiety
fields.risk_factors: Stress/anxiety; insulin resistance/diabetes and estrogen deficiency (proposed mechanisms)
fields.pathology: Proposed mechanisms as under etiology
fields.clinical: Angina with ST changes
fields.diagnosis: Diagnosis of exclusion; angiography required to rule out CAD (coronary artery disease)
fields.treatment: Similar to CAD (coronary artery disease): lifestyle/risk-factor reduction, calcium channel blocker, beta-blocker, ACE (angiotensin-converting enzyme) inhibitor, statin

lectures.title: Heart Failure
lectures.note: Classified per the 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA heart failure guideline (American Heart Association / American College of Cardiology / Heart Failure Society of America), per Dr. Carter; the deck's 2026 changes on slide 57 are left out.

conditions.name: Heart failure (the syndrome)
conditions.prof_note: Slide 32 flags Brain Natriuretic Peptide with '***'

fields.name: Heart failure (HF); congestive heart failure (CHF) as the clinical diagnosis
fields.definition: Heart cannot pump blood fast enough to meet metabolic demand at rest and with effort, or does so only with abnormally high filling pressures; a clinical syndrome (constellation of signs and symptoms) from any structural or functional disorder that impairs ventricular filling or ejection; clinical HF = HF symptoms plus elevated BNP (B-type natriuretic peptide) or objective cardiogenic congestion
fields.etiology: All HF has a cardiomyopathy etiology: ischemic cardiomyopathy (myocardial infarction, chronic ischemia, hypoperfusion/shock) vs non-ischemic (hypertension, valvular disease, most often aortic stenosis; dilated, hypertrophic, restrictive, peripartum, septic, arrhythmogenic, Takotsubo cardiomyopathy; congenital heart disease; toxins such as alcohol and chemotherapy; diabetes, thyroid disease, rheumatoid arthritis, lupus)
fields.epidemiology: 6.7 million Americans over 20 have HF (2025); 60% of patients are over 65; 10–15% of people over 80 have HF; lifetime risk 24% (1 in 4)
fields.risk_factors: Age; hypertension; coronary artery disease; diabetes; chronic tachyarrhythmias; obesity/metabolic syndrome; excess alcohol; tobacco; family history; genetic abnormality; cardiotoxic medications
fields.pathology: Four mechanisms: excess preload (volume), excess afterload (resistance), decreased contractility, decreased filling; injury → remodeling (myocyte hypertrophy, collagen fibrosis) driven by neurohormones (sympathetic system and RAAS (renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system) harmful; natriuretic peptides protective), inflammation, mechanical stress; compensation: ↑heart rate, ↑contractility, ↑preload
fields.clinical: Congestion: dyspnea, DOE (dyspnea on exertion), orthopnea (breathlessness lying flat), PND (paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea: waking breathless at night), pulmonary/peripheral edema, S3 and S4 gallops (extra heart sounds), elevated JVP (jugular venous pressure), hepatomegaly; low perfusion: fatigue, weakness, syncope, obtundation, cool extremities, narrow pulse pressure, low sodium, renal dysfunction; warm/cold and wet/dry profiles
fields.diagnosis: Clinical diagnosis: HF signs/symptoms + elevated BNP (B-type natriuretic peptide) or cardiogenic congestion; chest X-ray (pleural effusion, cephalization, Kerley B lines (short horizontal lines at the lung edges), ↑cardiothoracic ratio); echo (most accurate structures); MUGA (multigated acquisition scan; most accurate EF (ejection fraction)); CBC (complete blood count), CMP (comprehensive metabolic panel: potassium, renal function), troponin; ECG (electrocardiogram): ischemia, LVH (left ventricular hypertrophy), right heart strain; BNP <100 rules out acute HF, >400 likely HF; NT-proBNP (N-terminal pro-BNP) >125 under 75 y, >450 over 75 y likely HF
fields.treatment: Goals: fewer symptoms, longer survival, slower progression; GDMT (guideline-directed medical therapy): diuretics (hydrochlorothiazide, metolazone, furosemide, bumetanide), ACEi (angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor: lisinopril, enalapril), ARB (angiotensin receptor blocker: losartan, valsartan, irbesartan), ARNI (angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitor: valsartan/sacubitril), beta blocker (metoprolol, atenolol, propranolol), SGLT2i (sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor: dapagliflozin, empagliflozin), MRA (mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist: spironolactone, eplerenone), nitrates; avoid calcium channel blockers (deck: dihydropyridines contraindicated, non-dihydropyridines avoid); inotropes in the intensive care unit only; 2022 stages: A SGLT2i in diabetes; B SGLT2i in diabetes, ACEi (ARB if intolerant), beta blocker; ICD (implantable cardioverter-defibrillator) if LVEF (left ventricular ejection fraction) ≤35%, NYHA (New York Heart Association) II–III on optimal GDMT, life expectancy ≥1 y
fields.mortality: 1-year post-hospitalization mortality 35%; HF causes 45% of cardiovascular deaths (47% vs 29% for heart attack in 2022); each BNP (B-type natriuretic peptide) rise of 100 → 35% higher relative risk of death; predischarge BNP <430 → lower 30-day readmission

conditions.name: Left-sided heart failure
conditions.prof_note: Slide 8 lists 'Most common by far (70-80%)' under 'Important to know'

fields.name: Left heart failure (left-sided HF (heart failure))
fields.definition: Left ventricular involvement: systolic or diastolic failure; dilated, hypertrophic or restrictive cardiomyopathy; ischemic or non-ischemic; preserved or reduced EF (ejection fraction)
fields.etiology: As for all HF (heart failure): a cardiomyopathy etiology, ischemic or non-ischemic
fields.epidemiology: Most common type by far (70–80%); the main focus of the lecture
fields.pathology: Systolic dysfunction from ischemic/dilated cardiomyopathy, or diastolic dysfunction from hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (see HFrEF and HFpEF cards)
fields.clinical: S3 (rapid ventricular filling sound) and S4 (atrial contraction sound); systolic: normal/low blood pressure, S3, pulmonary edema; diastolic: hypertension, S4, peripheral then pulmonary edema
fields.diagnosis: Not covered in the lecture
fields.treatment: Not covered in the lecture

conditions.name: Right-sided heart failure

fields.name: Right heart failure (right-sided HF (heart failure))
fields.definition: HF of the right ventricle: systolic or diastolic failure; dilated, hypertrophic or restrictive cardiomyopathy; ischemic (right coronary artery) or non-ischemic; preserved or reduced EF (ejection fraction)
fields.etiology: Chronic left-sided HF (most common: left HF → right hypertrophic → right dilated cardiomyopathy); mitral valve stenosis; PAH (pulmonary artery hypertension)
fields.pathology: Same as left-sided HF; right ventricular failure = fluid backs up
fields.clinical: Systemic overload: peripheral edema, JVD (jugular venous distension); portal overload: nausea, loss of appetite, hepatomegaly (congestion/ascites); ± murmur: mitral stenosis (rumbling diastolic apical murmur with opening snap) or tricuspid regurgitation in PAH (pulmonary artery hypertension; holosystolic murmur at left lower sternal border)
fields.diagnosis: Clinical HF with JVD (jugular venous distension) suggests right-sided; echo (definitive, by EF (ejection fraction)); right heart catheterization (severity; PCWP (pulmonary capillary wedge pressure) 5–12 mmHg, pulmonary edema likely >20); ECG (electrocardiogram) right heart strain: right axis deviation, RBBB (right bundle branch block), T-wave inversion V1–V3
fields.treatment: Same as left-sided HF: symptom management, treat underlying cause, heart transplant, palliative care
fields.mortality: Prognosis much worse than left-sided HF

conditions.name: Systolic HF / HFrEF (including HFimpEF)
conditions.prof_note: Slide 56 marks the HFrEF GDMT summary 'REMEMBER!!!'

fields.name: Systolic heart failure; HFrEF (heart failure with reduced ejection fraction); HFimpEF (heart failure with improved ejection fraction)
fields.definition: Failure of systolic function (the squeeze): impaired contraction; HFrEF = LVEF (left ventricular ejection fraction) ≤40%; HFimpEF = LVEF ≤40% that improves to >40%; EF (ejection fraction) = stroke volume / end-diastolic volume × 100
fields.etiology: Ischemic cardiomyopathy or dilated cardiomyopathy
fields.pathology: Dilated cardiomyopathy: thin, dilated (ballooned) muscle; less muscle = poor contraction and loss of elasticity; decreased contractility
fields.clinical: Normal or low blood pressure; S3 (sound of rapid filling of the dilated left ventricle); pulmonary edema
fields.diagnosis: Reduced EF (ejection fraction, ≤40%) on echo (MUGA (multigated acquisition scan) most accurate EF); add an elevated BNP (B-type natriuretic peptide) = "slam dunk"
fields.treatment: GDMT (guideline-directed medical therapy): beta blocker, RAS-i (renin-angiotensin system inhibitor), MRA (mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist), SGLT2i (sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor), prioritized for comorbidities; 2022 figure (all class 1): ARNI (angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitor) in NYHA (New York Heart Association) II–III or ACEi/ARB (angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor / angiotensin receptor blocker) in II–IV, beta blocker, MRA, SGLT2i, diuretics as needed, hydralazine-nitrates for NYHA III–IV in African American patients; ICD (implantable cardioverter-defibrillator) if LVEF ≤35%, NYHA II–III on optimal GDMT, life expectancy ≥1 y; acute HF with EF <35% → LifeVest (wearable defibrillator) → optimize GDMT + cardiac rehab → recheck echo → ICD if not improved
fields.mortality: 52% of cardiac arrests in hospitalized HFrEF patients are due to ventricular arrhythmias

fields.name: Diastolic heart failure; HFpEF (heart failure with preserved ejection fraction)
fields.definition: Failure of diastolic function (the rest): impaired relaxation; HFpEF = LVEF (left ventricular ejection fraction) ≥50%
fields.etiology: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (hypertension → hypertrophy)
fields.pathology: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy: enlarged, thickened muscle; more muscle = strong contraction but poor relaxation; decreased filling; echo LVH (left ventricular hypertrophy) = wall >10 mm
fields.clinical: Hypertension; S4 (strong left atrial contraction against a stiff hypertrophic left ventricle); peripheral edema → pulmonary edema
fields.diagnosis: Preserved EF (ejection fraction, ≥50%) on echo; add an elevated BNP (B-type natriuretic peptide); ECG (electrocardiogram) LVH: tall R in V5–V6, deep S in V1–V2
fields.treatment: Diuretics as needed; beta blocker, RAS-i (renin-angiotensin system inhibitor), MRA (mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist), SGLT2i (sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor) for comorbidities; 2022 figure: diuretics (class 1), SGLT2i (2a), ARNI (angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitor), MRA, ARB (angiotensin receptor blocker) (2b)

fields.name: Acute HF (heart failure): acute new-onset HF, HF exacerbation, acute on chronic HF; decompensated HF
fields.definition: Acute = sudden, new onset or exacerbation (chronic = over 1 year); course: pre-HF (asymptomatic) → acute new-onset HF → resolution → exacerbation → chronic HF → acute on chronic HF; clinical HF is symptomatic and its diagnosis requires congestion (pulmonary and/or peripheral edema)
fields.etiology: Myocardial infarction, sepsis, acute renal failure, etc.
fields.pathology: Not covered in the lecture
fields.clinical: Congestion (edema); crackles; Forrester subsets (deck: "Swan-Forester"; by cardiac index 2.5 L/min/m² and wedge pressure 15 mmHg): I warm-dry, II warm-wet (congestion), III cool-dry (hypoperfusion), IV cool-wet
fields.diagnosis: BNP (B-type natriuretic peptide) rises in 1–3 h, peaks at 12 h, is degraded by neprilysin (affected by ARNI (angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitor)) and by chronic kidney disease; NT-proBNP (N-terminal pro-BNP) is more stable, peaks at 24 h, detected earlier and longer; BNP <100 rules out acute HF, >900 likely acute HF; NT-proBNP cut-off 300 rules out acute HF
fields.treatment: Inotropes in the ICU (intensive care unit) only: digitalis, dobutamine, norepinephrine, epinephrine, milrinone; diuretics; with EF (ejection fraction) <35% → LifeVest (wearable defibrillator) → optimize GDMT (guideline-directed medical therapy) + cardiac rehab → recheck echo → ICD (implantable cardioverter-defibrillator) if not improved
fields.mortality: 1-year post-hospitalization mortality 35%; each BNP (B-type natriuretic peptide) rise of 100 → 35% higher relative risk of death; predischarge BNP <430 → lower 30-day readmission

fields.name: High-output heart failure
fields.definition: Elevated cardiac output from increased heart rate and contractility
fields.etiology: Increased peripheral demand: anemia, hyperthyroidism, atrioventricular fistula
fields.risk_factors: Obesity; COPD (chronic obstructive pulmonary disease); cirrhosis; Paget disease (osteitis deformans)
fields.pathology: Increased demand may lead to ischemic cardiomyopathy or remodeling
fields.clinical: Heart failure syndrome: fatigue, dyspnea, edema, palpitations
fields.diagnosis: Echo; CBC (complete blood count); CMP (comprehensive metabolic panel); BNP (B-type natriuretic peptide)
fields.treatment: Treat the underlying cause; diuretic
